content: Phlegm is a viscous fluid secreted by the mucous membranes of animals. Its definition is specifically limited to the mucus produced by the respiratory system, excluding that from the nasal passages. It is particularly associated with the mucus expelled through coughing, known as sputum. The composition of phlegm can vary depending on factors such as climate, genetic predisposition, and the state of the immune system. However, it is fundamentally a water-based gel that contains glycoproteins, immunoglobulins, lipids, and other components. Historically, in Hippocratic medicine and for centuries thereafter, phlegm was considered one of the four bodily humours. It was thought to possess the qualities of coldness and wetness and was believed to be responsible for apathetic and sluggish behavior. This historical perspective is reflected in the term phlegmatic. Phlegm can present in various colors, each of which may indicate different underlying conditions: Clear or white phlegm is generally considered healthy. Yellow phlegm often signifies an infection. During the early stages of a common cold or flu, when the phlegm is still clear, the individual is most contagious. As the phlegm turns yellow, it indicates that the body is actively combating the infection. Greenish or brownish phlegm is almost always indicative of an infection. Greenish or rusty-colored phlegm, or phlegm with rusty spots, may suggest pneumonia or internal micro-bleeding. Brown phlegm is commonly associated with smoking. This occurs due to the accumulation of resin in the phlegm, which is then expelled by the body. Another type of phlegm linked to smoking is brownish-gray in color. This variant is often encased in clear saliva. When spread out, the brown-gray core appears grainy rather than cohesive. This type of phlegm may contain dust and other foreign particles and is often seen in individuals with damaged cilia, such as those with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Phlegm can also serve as a carrier for larvae of intestinal parasites, such as hookworms. The presence of blood in sputum can be a symptom of serious conditions like tuberculosis or lung cancer. However, it can also be a relatively benign symptom of minor illnesses, such as bronchitis, in which the sputum may be lightly streaked with blood. Coughing up significant amounts of blood is always a serious medical condition and warrants immediate medical attention. In some cases, blood in phlegm may result from a nosebleed, where blood has drained into the throat and mixed with the mucus. In the context of humourism, an ancient medical theory, the human body was believed to be governed by four fundamental substances, known as the four humours. These humours were thought to correspond to the four classical elements: earth, fire, water, and air. The four humours were black bile, yellow bile, phlegm, and blood. Health was believed to result from a balance among these humours, while disease and disability were attributed to an excess or deficiency of one of them.
